spec.title: Tailscale2OTel — Exporter health
spec.description: tailscale2otel's own health, organised by pipeline stage: collection, ingestion, delivery, runtime, and cost/cardinality. Open this when a panel on tailscale2otel-tailnet is empty and you need to know whether the tailnet is quiet or the exporter is broken. Generated by deploy/grafana/gen/build.py.

spec.name: log_event
spec.label: Log event
spec.query: All : .+, audit : tailscale.config.audit, flow : tailscale.network.flow, posture : tailscale.device.posture, key expiring : tailscale.key.expiring, webhook : tailscale.webhook.*

spec.title: Build info
spec.description: Version / Go version (labels).

spec.title: Scrape duration p50/p95/p99 by collector
spec.description: Per-collector scrape wall-clock duration quantiles (exemplars enabled — link a bucket back to the scrape trace). Supersedes the plain scrape-duration gauge panel (#369).

spec.title: Last scrape age
spec.description: Seconds since each collector's last scrape.

spec.title: API retries/s by endpoint
spec.description: Tailscale API calls retried (429/5xx/timeout), by endpoint.

spec.title: Export failures/s by type
spec.description: OTLP export attempts that failed, by error type.

spec.title: Active series by metric (top $topn)
spec.description: Per-metric active series (cap 10k). Watch the flow families.

spec.title: Memory breakdown
spec.description: Go memory obtained from the OS (runtime.memory.sys), stacked into in-use heap, idle/reserved heap, stacks, and other non-heap runtime (GC, mspan/mcache). Total height = total sys.

spec.title: GC next-target vs live heap
spec.description: Live heap vs the heap size that triggers the next GC; the gap is GC headroom.

spec.title: Heap alloc churn
spec.description: Cumulative heap-allocation rate (includes freed); allocation churn / GC pressure.

spec.title: Live heap objects
spec.description: Number of live heap objects (a count, despite the _ratio suffix).

spec.title: Scrape errors/s
spec.description: Collector scrape attempts that failed, by collector.

spec.title: Checkpoint persist errors/s
spec.description: Checkpoint-store writes that failed, by collector.

spec.title: Component errors/s
spec.description: Internal component errors, by component.

spec.title: Admin auth rejected/s
spec.description: Admin-endpoint requests rejected by auth, by reason.

spec.title: Config valid
spec.description: Whether the running config passed validation at startup.

spec.title: Config warnings
spec.description: Active configuration advisories from startup (a count, despite the _ratio suffix).

spec.title: Uptime
spec.description: Time since the process started.

spec.title: Checkpoint disk
spec.description: On-disk size of the file-backed checkpoint store.

defaults.noValue: No checkpoint file — the store is not file-backed, or nothing has persisted yet.

spec.title: Process CPU (user/system)
spec.description: CPU seconds/s by mode (~cores).

spec.title: Checkpoint persist age
spec.description: Absent when the checkpoint store is not file-backed (in-memory).

defaults.noValue: No checkpoint file — the store is not file-backed, or nothing has persisted yet.

spec.title: API latency p50/p95/p99 by endpoint
spec.description: Per-endpoint API latency quantiles (exemplars enabled).

spec.title: API 429 / retries
spec.description: Rate-limit responses and the retries they trigger, fleet-wide.

spec.title: Export latency p50/p95/p99 by signal
spec.description: OTLP export latency quantiles, by signal (metrics/logs/traces).

spec.title: Export outcome rate
spec.description: OTLP export attempts completed per second, by outcome (success/failure).

spec.title: Scrape staleness
spec.description: Time since each collector's last successful scrape.

spec.title: Scrape budget headroom
spec.description: Last scrape duration as a fraction of the collector's poll interval; near or above 1 means the scrape risks overrunning its interval.

spec.title: rDNS cache fill
spec.description: rDNS cache entries as a fraction of configured capacity.

spec.title: rDNS lookup hit-rate
spec.description: Share of rDNS lookups served from cache rather than an upstream query. 'of which stale' is the part served past its TTL while a refresh ran (enrichment.reverse_dns.stale_ttl) — those names are still correct, just older than cache_ttl.

spec.title: rDNS upstream queries/s
spec.description: Upstream PTR queries issued and cache evictions, per second. The refresh series are the subset of those queries triggered by a stale-serving hit.

spec.title: rDNS cache overflows vs lookups/s
spec.description: An overflow is a hot-path miss for a NEW address that could not be scheduled because the cache was already at enrichment.reverse_dns.max_entries — the address is simply never resolved. Read it against the accepted lookup rate: a sustained non-zero share means max_entries is too small.

defaults.noValue: No reverse-DNS cache series. Requires enrichment.reverse_dns.enabled and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: PII filter status
spec.description: Compliance view: every category should read 'emitted' (==1) unless redacted.

spec.title: Per-tailnet API errors
spec.description: Tailscale API 4xx/5xx responses per second, split out per tailnet on a multi-tailnet deployment.

spec.title: Object-store cursor age
spec.description: End-to-end ingestion lag: now minus the timestamp the last cycle left persisted. In a healthy feed it settles near the export's write cadence plus one collection interval. Never absent, never negative; a cold start reports the configured initial lookback rather than zero.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Newest exported object age
spec.description: How fresh the EXPORT's own writes are, independent of what was ingested — objects skipped as already ingested still count. -1 means the cycle listed no object with a usable timestamp (an empty or misconfigured prefix, or an export quieter than the listing window reaches); it is deliberately distinguishable from a fresh zero-second age.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Object-store gaps clear
spec.description: One when no unresolved gap remains; zero means at least one pending or quarantined object is outstanding.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Object listing complete
spec.description: One means unexamined listing ground remains after the last cycle (a truncated S3 page, or a listed object not yet durably handled), which makes the backlog and oldest-pending-age panels lower bounds rather than totals.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Backlog & oldest pending object age
spec.description: Objects listed but NOT YET ingested, and how stale the next one to be processed already is. This is the waiting population only — an object that fails leaves it for the gap panel — so zero here pairs with a zero backlog and means nothing is queued. Both are lower bounds while the listing is truncated.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Unresolved gaps & oldest gap age
spec.description: FAILED objects awaiting retry or operator acknowledgement, and the age of the oldest. A different question from the pending backlog and a different population: this one ages objects that already failed, and a gap aging without the count falling is an object failing repeatedly rather than recovering.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Objects & records ingested/s
spec.description: Objects fully ingested and flow-log records decoded out of them. Compare the record rate against the flow metrics to see what de-duplication removed.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Object bytes read vs decompressed
spec.description: Transfer cost (compressed bytes actually read, including unsuccessful attempts) against expansion (decompressed bytes consumed, including attempts stopped by a limit). Use THESE two for object-store cost and expansion, not tailscale2otel.ingest.size — that one now reports decoded payload bytes for every source so it can be summed across sources.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Object retries/s
spec.description: OBJECT-level retries: a failed object becomes a durable gap and is attempted again on a later cycle under a bounded backoff. There is no transport-level retry here, and a first attempt on a newly listed object never counts. Emitted every cycle including zero, so a flat line is a healthy feed.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Objects skipped/s by reason
spec.description: Objects or individual rows not ingested. `decode_error` and `semantic_invalid` are single rows discarded from an object that still completed; a sustained `per_cycle_budget` means the per-cycle object cap is holding ingestion behind the bucket; `future_timestamp` means objects are named beyond the 5-minute clock-skew allowance — check the export's clock.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Undecodable objects (broken feed)
spec.description: Whole objects that decoded ZERO records while at least one row failed — the signature of an export whose framing is not newline-delimited records. Treat ANY non-zero value as a feed-level fault, not as corrupt data: the entire object is discarded and becomes a retried gap. Reading note: for a wholly failed object the row-local decode_error/semantic_invalid reasons are deliberately not emitted, so it shows as ONE undecodable_object rather than N decode_error.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Expansion limit failures/s by limit
spec.description: Ingestion attempts stopped by a configured wire-byte, decompressed-byte or record-count budget. The bounded `limit` attribute names which object or cycle limit was breached.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Object-store provider requests/s
spec.description: TRANSPORT health only, and at most four series. `error` means the LIST or GET call itself returned an error — never a decode, validation, framing or limit failure, which the skipped and gap panels carry. A body that fails mid-read counts as a SUCCESSFUL get here.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Object-store provider latency p50/p95/p99
spec.description: Times the provider call itself. For `get` that is obtaining the object's reader — NOT streaming, decompressing and decoding its body, which the object, record and byte counters measure.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Ingress WAL pending & retained entries
spec.description: Durable entries awaiting processor application and flush, staging files kept for bounded recovery cleanup, and transient completion markers awaiting durable cleanup. All three are counts despite the _ratio suffix. Pending climbing toward ingress_wal.max_entries fails new requests closed.

defaults.noValue: No ingress-WAL series. Requires ingress_wal.enabled together with a receiver that accepts payloads (streaming or webhook), and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Ingress WAL on-disk bytes
spec.description: Encoded bytes on the WAL filesystem. There is no TTL or eviction, so this is bounded only by ingress_wal.max_bytes — reaching it fails new requests closed.

defaults.noValue: No ingress-WAL series. Requires ingress_wal.enabled together with a receiver that accepts payloads (streaming or webhook), and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Subrequest attempts/s
spec.description: Per-entity calls made inside a scrape (one posture-attributes call per device, and so on) — the N+1 cost that a single scrape-duration figure hides.

defaults.noValue: No per-entity subrequest series. Requires a collector that fans out per entity — devices posture attributes, device invites, or user invites — and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Subrequest failures/s by API state
spec.description: A single entity's subrequest failing is non-fatal to the enclosing snapshot, so the collector still reports a clean scrape while coverage degrades. A scope_denied state here is a missing OAuth scope, not a transient error.

defaults.noValue: No per-entity subrequest series. Requires a collector that fans out per entity — devices posture attributes, device invites, or user invites — and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Subrequest coverage (last pass)
spec.description: Fraction of per-entity subrequests that succeeded on the last pass — a genuine ratio, unlike most _ratio metrics here. 1 when nothing was attempted: an empty tailnet has complete coverage of the entities it has.

defaults.noValue: No per-entity subrequest series. Requires a collector that fans out per entity — devices posture attributes, device invites, or user invites — and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Capability state by collector
spec.description: The current state of each enabled collector, filtered to the state that is set. Read it before believing an empty operational panel: `disabled` means the tailnet does not have the feature, `scope_denied` means the credential cannot see it. The value is the most operator-relevant state across that collector's probed operations, so a partial scope_denied is never masked by a sibling success.

defaults.noValue: No capability-preflight series. Requires self_observability.enabled; the scope preflight additionally requires tailscale.auth.method: oauth, as an API key carries no scope list to compare against.

spec.title: OAuth scope preflight by capability
spec.description: Advisory STARTUP preflight, not a server answer: it compares the configured tailscale.auth.oauth.scopes against a static map of upstream's documented requirements, never blocks collection, and a `satisfied` is not a guarantee. Emitted only for capabilities whose scope is modelled and only under an OAuth client. The authoritative signal is the capability state reaching scope_denied.

defaults.noValue: No capability-preflight series. Requires self_observability.enabled; the scope preflight additionally requires tailscale.auth.method: oauth, as an API key carries no scope list to compare against.

spec.title: API operation availability by state
spec.description: Per-OPERATION availability, the finer-grained sibling of the capability table above: that one reports the most operator-relevant state across a collector, this one names which individual API operation is in it. Filtered to the state that is set — the full state set is zero-seeded and always emitted, so a state that stops occurring reads as 0 rather than vanishing, and an unfiltered table would be mostly zeroes. This is the metric the descriptions of tailscale.acl.validation.ok and tailscale.webhook_endpoints.count point at when they say an under-scoped credential emits nothing rather than a zero.

defaults.noValue: No capability-preflight series. Requires self_observability.enabled; the scope preflight additionally requires tailscale.auth.method: oauth, as an API key carries no scope list to compare against.

spec.title: Rate-limiter wait p50/p95/p99 by endpoint
spec.description: Time a request spent blocked on the CLIENT-side limiter (tailscale.http.rate_limit) before its first attempt. A rising distribution means the configured limit is throttling the poller: raise rate_limit or lengthen collector intervals. Compare against the collector interval — wait approaching it means scrapes will start overlapping.

defaults.noValue: No rate-limiter wait recorded. Requires tailscale.http.rate_limit (or a per-tailnet http.rate_limit) above 0 and at least one request that actually blocked — a request that waits zero is never recorded.

spec.title: Time waiting vs time on the wire
spec.description: Seconds spent per second in each budget. The two do not overlap — api.duration records genuine API/network plus backoff time and excludes the limiter wait — so wait exceeding wire time means the exporter is mostly queueing against its own limit rather than waiting on Tailscale.

defaults.noValue: No rate-limiter wait recorded. Requires tailscale.http.rate_limit (or a per-tailnet http.rate_limit) above 0 and at least one request that actually blocked — a request that waits zero is never recorded.

spec.title: Requests delayed by the rate limiter
spec.description: Share of API requests that actually blocked. Only requests that waited are recorded — a zero-wait request is skipped — so the histogram count is the delayed population and the request counter is the whole one.

defaults.noValue: No rate-limiter wait recorded. Requires tailscale.http.rate_limit (or a per-tailnet http.rate_limit) above 0 and at least one request that actually blocked — a request that waits zero is never recorded.

spec.title: API operation last-probe age
spec.description: Seconds since each API operation was last probed. A row aging past its collector's interval means that operation stopped being exercised, which is how a capability state goes stale without anything erroring.

defaults.noValue: No API probe timestamps. Requires self_observability.enabled and at least one collector that has probed an API operation.

spec.title: Stream records accepted vs skipped/s
spec.description: Skipped records were extracted from an otherwise-valid body and then never routed to a processor: `unclassified` matched neither the flow nor the audit shape, `unwrap_drop` was a non-object HEC event dropped while unwrapping. Read against the accepted rate — a bare skip count says nothing about how much of the feed is being lost.

defaults.noValue: No streaming-receiver series. Requires streaming.enabled with collectors.flowlogs.source or collectors.auditlogs.source set to stream.

spec.title: Receiver rejections/s by reason
spec.description: WHOLE requests refused before any record was extracted, by bounded reason (bad token, no token on a reachable bind, body over cap, bad HMAC). Distinct from skipped records, which came out of a request that was accepted.

defaults.noValue: No streaming-receiver series. Requires streaming.enabled with collectors.flowlogs.source or collectors.auditlogs.source set to stream.

spec.title: Webhook request duration p50/p95/p99
spec.description: Wall-clock handling time for webhook deliveries. Tailscale retries a delivery it considers timed out, so a rising tail here turns into duplicate events rather than lost ones.

defaults.noValue: No webhook-receiver series. Requires webhook.enabled and at least one Tailscale webhook endpoint delivering to it.

spec.title: Webhook events accepted vs duplicates/s
spec.description: Accepted volume for the duration and rejection panels above, alongside the redeliveries the dedup failsafe suppressed.

defaults.noValue: No webhook-receiver series. Requires webhook.enabled and at least one Tailscale webhook endpoint delivering to it.

spec.title: Webhook payload schema drift/s by field
spec.description: Webhook event schema observations by field and known status. A field moving to an unknown status means Tailscale changed the payload shape: the receiver keeps accepting the event, so nothing else here goes red, but whatever the drifted field feeds is quietly no longer populated. Read it alongside the accepted volume above — drift on a field nobody consumes is noise, drift on one that is charted is a silent data loss.

defaults.noValue: No webhook-receiver series. Requires webhook.enabled and at least one Tailscale webhook endpoint delivering to it.

spec.title: Scrape → API trace waterfall
spec.description: Trace panels are empty if tracing.enabled=false.

spec.title: API p95 by endpoint (traces)
spec.description: Trace panels are empty if tracing.enabled=false.

spec.title: Scrape cadence by collector (traces)
spec.description: Trace panels are empty if tracing.enabled=false.

spec.title: stream.receive batch size (traces)
spec.description: Trace panels are empty if tracing.enabled=false.

spec.title: Metrics over cardinality cap
spec.description: Metric families that exceeded the per-metric series cap (cardinality.metric_limit, default 10000) and are now collapsing excess series into one otel_metric_overflow series — SILENT per-series detail loss. >0 means raise metric_limit or lower flow cardinality (ephemeral source_port is the biggest driver).

spec.title: Busiest metric — % of cap
spec.description: Highest per-metric active-series count as a fraction of the 10k cap.

spec.title: Total active series
spec.description: Sum of active series across all tailscale2otel metrics (a proxy for ingest cost).

spec.title: Overflowing families
spec.description: Metric families currently over the per-metric cap (otel_metric_overflow=true).

defaults.noValue: No metrics over cap — all series fully resolved.

spec.title: Active series vs 10k cap (top $topn)
spec.description: Per-metric active series against the cap. Watch the flow families.

spec.title: Flow series: raw vs bounded rollup
spec.description: Raw flow families saturate the 10k cap; the bounded rollup stays small. When raw is at cap, trust the ROLLUP talker panels on the Network tab.

spec.title: __other__ rollup share
spec.description: Fraction of rollup bytes folded into the bounded __other__ bucket. High = many small talkers.

spec.title: Flow log records dropped/s
spec.description: Flow LOG records suppressed by the per-window volume guard (collectors.flowlogs.max_log_records_per_window). Metrics are never dropped, only logs.

spec.title: Dedup set size
spec.description: Keys held in each cross-source de-duplication set (a count).

spec.title: Dedup evictions/s
spec.description: Steady-state evictions are normal: dedup keys are effectively unique, so a full set evicts one key per insert forever even when healthy. Only evictions approaching a set's capacity within one poll interval indicate real overlap loss (boundary double-counting).

spec.title: Series limit
spec.description: Configured per-metric series limit (cardinality.metric_limit). 0 means unlimited.

defaults.noValue: No per-metric series cap reported — needs cardinality.metric_limit set (unset means unlimited) and exporter self-observability.

spec.title: Overflowing now
spec.description: Number of metric families currently overflowing their series cap. >0 means detail loss.

spec.title: Per-metric headroom (top-N)
spec.description: Per-metric active-series count divided by the series limit — headroom as a fraction. 1.0 = at cap. Uses / on() group_left() because the limit is a single unlabelled series.

spec.expr: topk($topn, max by (metric_name) (tailscale2otel_series_active) / on() group_left() max(tailscale2otel_series_limit))

spec.title: Active series by group
spec.description: Active series aggregated by metric_group — the primary cost-driver view. 18 groups live; each group maps to a logical collector domain.

spec.title: Metrics overflowing now
spec.description: Metric families where overflowing_ratio == 1 (capped). 147+ series tracked; 0 overflowing is the normal live state — that is correct.

defaults.noValue: No metrics overflowing.

spec.title: Ingest vs export cost (per minute)
spec.description: Export datapoints/min and log records/min (ingest cost) alongside per-source ingest rate. Rising DPM driven by a single source → check that group in 'Active series by group'.

spec.title: Forwarded metric-name drops/s by reason
spec.description: Samples dropped because their metric NAME had not been seen before and the distinct-name budget (node_metrics.max_distinct_metrics, default 2000) was already exhausted. Targets choose their own names and each new one creates a permanent instrument, so the budget is a hard bound on a node-controlled input. Read the drop rate against the active uncataloged series count on the right axis: that is the population the budget governs. Sustained drops mean raising max_distinct_metrics or tightening metric_allow/metric_deny.

defaults.noValue: No node-metrics name-budget series. Requires node_metrics.enabled with at least one target, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Metric names dropped over the window
spec.description: Total forwarded samples lost to the distinct-name budget over the dashboard's time range. Any non-zero value means a scrape target is presenting more distinct metric names than the budget allows.

defaults.noValue: No node-metrics name-budget series. Requires node_metrics.enabled with at least one target, and self_observability.enabled.
